meta.topic: Kitchen gaps: cheapest blender, slow cooker and stick blender by market; MET values for kitchen activities; an authoritative ingredient substitution table; time spent cooking
meta.method: Retail prices were read on the retailer's own pages: Target product and search pages through WebFetch; Walmart Mexico's search page and Liverpool's search and product pages through curl, reading the embedded page data; DID Electrical's Shopify collection JSON (did.ie/collections/<c>/products.json); Best Buy Canada's own JSON search and product API (bestbuy.ca/api/v2/json). Walmart.com, Walmart.ca, Canadian Tire, Argos (UK and IE), Harvey Norman IE, Currys and Tesco refused scripted requests (403 or bot check), so Argos UK figures come from search-engine snippets of argos.co.uk pages and are marked confirmed false. 'Cheapest' means cheapest found in the listings read, which for search pages is the first pages of results, not a full catalogue crawl. MET values were read on pacompendium.com's own heading pages. Substitutions were transcribed from the NDSU Extension PDF FN198. Time-use figures were read in the BLS ATUS Table A-1 2025 PDF, the ONS bulletin, and the StatCan table 45-10-0104 CSV. Nothing was estimated.
meta.taxConvention: taxIncluded is the market's shelf-price convention, not a line read on each product page: US and Canadian shelf prices exclude sales tax/GST/HST; UK, Irish and Mexican consumer prices are shown tax-inclusive (VAT, IVA). Treat these as background, not as figures confirmed on the page.

substitutionsSource.title: Ingredient Substitutions (FN198, reviewed Jan. 2023)
substitutionsSource.publisher: NDSU Extension, North Dakota State University
substitutionsSource.author: Julie Garden-Robinson, Ph.D., R.D., L.R.D.; original authors Nancy Brockel Kaufman and Pat Beck
substitutionsSource.licence: Creative Commons, non-commercial, attribution, share-alike (stated on page 12)
substitutionsSource.caveat: The publication says substitution may alter taste, colour, moisture or texture, and recommends it for unexpected situations only.
substitutionsSource.units: US customary (1 cup = 16 tablespoons = 48 teaspoons per the PDF's own 'Measuring Up' page)

substitutions.note: Also listed: 7/8 cup oil alone; 7/8 cup lard + 1/2 tsp salt; 7/8 to 1 cup hydrogenated fat + 1/2 tsp salt.

substitutions.substitute: reconstituted nonfat dry milk plus butter or margarine
substitutions.substituteAmount: 1 cup reconstituted nonfat dry milk + 2 1/2 tsp butter or margarine
1 cup buttermilk + 1/2 tsp baking soda; decrease baking powder by 2 tsp

substitutions.note: Also: 1 cup fruit juice or potato water (in baking); 4 tbsp whole dry milk + 1 cup water; 1/4 cup nonfat dry milk + 7/8 cup water + 2 tsp butter or margarine.

substitutions.substitute: dry whole egg powder plus water
substitutions.substituteAmount: 2 1/2 tbsp sifted dry whole egg powder + 2 1/2 tbsp lukewarm water

substitutions.note: Also: 2 yolks + 1 tbsp water (in cookies); 2 yolks (in custards, cream fillings).
Listed under 'Egg substitute'. For recipes calling for 2 or 3 eggs, per egg: 2 tbsp flour, 1/2 tbsp shortening, 1/2 tsp baking powder, 2 tbsp of the recipe's liquid.

substitutions.substitute: sweet milk plus lemon juice or vinegar
substitutions.substituteAmount: 1 cup minus 1 tbsp milk + 1 tbsp lemon juice or vinegar; stand 5 to 10 minutes

substitutions.substitute: sweet milk plus cream of tartar
substitutions.substituteAmount: 1 cup milk + 1 3/4 tsp cream of tartar
1 cup (in cooking add 1 tbsp cornstarch per cup to prevent separating)

substitutions.substitute: sour milk or buttermilk plus butter or margarine
cottage cheese plus lemon juice, pureed
substitutions.substituteAmount: 1 cup cottage cheese + 2 or 3 tsp lemon juice
substitutions.note: Also: 3/4 cup milk + 3/4 tsp lemon juice + 1/3 cup butter; 1 cup evaporated milk at 70°F + 1 tbsp vinegar, left to clabber. The 'Cream, sour' row adds 3 tbsp butter + 7/8 cup sour milk, or 7/8 cup buttermilk + 3 tbsp butter.

substitutions.substitute: milk plus butter or margarine (cooking and baking)
substitutions.substituteAmount: 3/4 cup milk + 1/3 cup butter or margarine

substitutions.note: Also: evaporated skim milk, or equal parts part-skim ricotta and nonfat yogurt beaten smooth (cannot be heated).

substitutions.substitute: whole milk plus butter or margarine
substitutions.substituteAmount: 7/8 cup whole milk + 1/2 tbsp butter or margarine
substitutions.note: Also: 1 cup evaporated milk; 3 tbsp oil + milk to 1 cup.

Also: 1 cup cottage cheese blended smooth; 1 cup sour cream. The PDF's layout puts '1 packaged (1/4 ounce) active dry yeast' as the first bullet beside Yogurt; it belongs to the Yeast row above and is omitted here.
Also: 1/4 cup chopped fresh onion; 1 1/3 tsp onion salt; 1 to 2 tbsp minced (dried) onion.

substitutions.substitute: garlic powder or instant minced garlic
substitutions.substituteAmount: 1/8 tsp garlic powder or 1/4 tsp instant minced garlic

substitutions.note: Row 'Lemon'. Also: 1 medium lemon = 2 to 3 tbsp lemon juice + 1 to 2 tsp rind.

substitutions.substituteAmount: 1 bouillon cube dissolved in 1 cup boiling water

substitutions.substitute: powdered broth base in boiling water
substitutions.substituteAmount: 1 tsp powdered broth base in 1 cup boiling water

substitutions.substitute: cornstarch, potato starch, rice starch or arrowroot
substitutions.note: Also: 2 to 3 tsp quick-cooking tapioca; 1 1/2 tbsp whole wheat flour; 2 tbsp browned flour.

substitutions.substitute: all-purpose flour plus baking powder and salt
substitutions.substituteAmount: 1 cup minus 2 tsp all-purpose flour + 1 1/2 tsp baking powder + 1/2 tsp salt
replace 1/4 to 1/2 of the white flour
substitutions.note: Specialty-flour swaps (rye 1 1/4 cups, rice flour 3/4 cup, oat flour 1 1/2 cups, etc.) need 2 1/2 tsp baking powder per cup; reduce yeast-bread volume.

substitutions.substituteAmount: 1 cup; decrease recipe liquid by 1/4 cup; in baking add 1/2 tsp baking soda per cup and lower oven 25 degrees
3/4 cup; reduce recipe liquid by 3 tbsp
substitutions.note: Also: 2 cups corn syrup (reduce liquid 1/4 cup; never more than half the sugar); 1 3/4 cups confectioners' sugar (not for baking).

substitutions.substitute: baking soda plus cream of tartar
substitutions.substituteAmount: 1/4 tsp baking soda + 5/8 tsp cream of tartar
substitutions.note: The PDF also lists 1/3 tsp baking soda + 1/2 tsp cream of tartar.

substitutions.substitute: cooked bulgur wheat or pearl barley

notFound: Walmart.com (US): bot check on every page; Target used instead.
Walmart.ca and Canadian Tire: bot check / 403; Best Buy Canada used instead.
Argos UK: 403 to WebFetch and curl; figures come from search snippets only (confirmed false); wattages not read.
Argos.ie and Harvey Norman IE: 403; DID Electrical used instead.
Walmart México slow cooker: the search page hit a bot check on the second request; the product pages too. Walmart MX blender and stick-blender wattage and capacity not read.
Wattage for the DID Morphy Richards 6.5L slow cooker, the Best Buy Hamilton Beach 6Qt, the Liverpool Chefman, and both Argos items: not stated on the pages read.
Statistics Canada meal-preparation minutes: table 45-10-0104 has no meal-preparation row (only 'Unpaid household work').
Average time to cook a single meal: no official source publishes a per-meal figure; ATUS and ONS publish minutes per day.
worthChecking: Best Buy Canada's Hamilton Beach model 33463 is titled 6Qt but its description says '7 litre capacity'.

Retail 'cheapest' covers the first pages of each retailer's search, sorted by price where the site allowed it (Target, Walmart MX); Liverpool and DID were sorted locally from the pages fetched. A full category crawl could find a cheaper item.
Several Liverpool and Best Buy items are sold by marketplace sellers, not the retailer itself; each entry names the seller.
NDSU FN198 is US customary and US-product-specific (e.g. Sugar Twin, Equal); UK/IE/MX markets may need metric conversion or local equivalents.

Only NDSU FN198 was transcribed. Canada's Food Guide and the other named extension tables (Penn State, Clemson, Utah State, Iowa State) were not read; Utah State's list (https://extension.usu.edu/archive/list-of-ingredient-substitutions-for-cooking-and-baking) and a University of Arkansas PDF came up in search and could cross-check it.
